task.title: Materialize the latest due recurrence through the CLI
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/923 by exposing atomic latest-due occurrence and task materialization through a deterministic writable CLI adapter.
acceptance_criteria: Validate recurrence identity, numeric inputs, and caller-owned task identity before writable storage access.
Delegate selection and atomic occurrence-task binding to the kernel and emit deterministic compact JSON with exact cursor semantics.
Preserve future write-free behavior and all-or-nothing rollback with one stable diagnostic and no partial stdout on failure.

attempts.diagnostic: The focused CLI integration test failed because materialize-latest-due was an unrecognized recurrence subcommand.
attempts.patch: Added tests for success, future and finite horizons, invalid inputs, storage-open failures, selected corruption, collisions, and rollback before dispatch existed.

attempts.diagnostic: Added minimal parsing and dispatch that delegates the observed revision, start, cutoff, and exact task identity to materialize_latest_due_occurrence and serializes the complete binding.
attempts.patch: Implemented the command in crates/vela-dev/src/lib.rs and documented its bounded authority in ADR-0065.

attempts.summary: Completed independent and substantive exact-head review.
attempts.diagnostic: Independent review prompted explicit storage-open and selected-corruption tests. CodeRabbit completed a genuine six-file review with no actionable comments and zero review threads; exact head c7ea529982b4f5c82ffbee630adc0ecf2d585354 passed the Rust quality gate.
attempts.patch: Reused the existing materialized-occurrence projection, kept transaction policy in the kernel, strengthened failure coverage, and reran the complete repository gate.

outcome.summary: Operators can bind one caller-owned task to the latest caller-selected due occurrence without the CLI acquiring clock, identity, scheduler-policy, permission, or execution authority.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- record validate corpus/development/0191-atomic-latest-due-recurrence-materialization-cli.json # result: valid development record
nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- corpus inspect corpus/development # result: inspected 193 records: 193 valid, 0 invalid
Pull request 924 exact head c7ea529982b4f5c82ffbee630adc0ecf2d585354 squash merge 80a56713f367bc592f030ae30630510a933083b4

lessons: A CLI adapter should accept a complete task identity from its caller rather than generate identity implicitly.
Storage-open and selected-corruption failures deserve explicit adapter-level coverage because both must preserve empty stdout and rollback.
Shared materialized-occurrence serialization keeps kernel and CLI evidence shapes aligned.
The command creates durable inert state but grants no claim, lease, dispatch, retry, workflow, provider, tool, permission, or execution authority.
